newsitem.title: USA: Dow index extends romp through 7,000, setting new high.
newsitem.headline: Dow index extends romp through 7,000, setting new high.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks sprinted to another record high Tuesday, resuming last week's fast-paced rise with the help of a burst of merger activity.
The Dow Jones industrial average ended up 78.50 points at 7,067.46 after closing above the 7,000 level for the first time ever last Thursday.
It was the 13th record close so far this year for the 30-stock blue-chip index as big-name companies extended their run as the favoured class on Wall Street.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,509 to 1,036 on moderate volume of 474 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Standard & Poor's 500 stock index and NYSE Composite index also ended in record territory.
Analysts said a number of factors played into the rally, including the flurry of merger deals, and, somewhat ironically, a heightened sense of caution about the market.
"People are cautious," said Peter Coolidge, senior equity trader at Brean Murray & Co. "People are buying quality. People are buying more liquid names."
Keeping with a recent trend, the session was fairly uneventful until the final moments, when a wave of programme buying propelled the Dow sharply higher.
Analysts said the dollar's recent strength also figured in the stock market's rally.

"With the dollar acting as well as it has, foreign investors have stepped up their buying," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co. "They tend to focus on the large-cap stocks because they're more liquid."

Currency traders called time out in the dollar's rally, as the currency fell from its highest level in nearly three years against the mark and the German currency benefited from a slump in both the Italian lira and British pound.

Mounting fears that Italy will not be a member of the first group of European nations forming a single currency and fading expectations for a Bank of England interest rate rise caused the currencies of those nations to drop.

After reaching a new high of 1.7050 German marks, the dollar fell to 1.6850 marks in late U.S. trading from 1.7015 at Monday's European close. The U.S. market was closed Monday for the Presidents Day holiday.
Leading the Dow's advance was Philip Morris Cos., which jumped 5-7/8 to 131-3/8 on speculation that tobacco companies were working together toward a broad settlement of lawsuits against the industry.
Other tobacco companies also posted sharp gains. RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp. rose 1-7/8 to 37-3/8, and UST Inc. gained one to 31-3/4.
Other strong Dow components were Procter & Gamble Co., up 4-3/8 to 129-1/4, and Boeing Co., up 2-1/4 to 110.
Elsewhere, the session was marked by a flurry of merger news led by H.F. Ahmanson & Co.'s surprise $6.0 billion stock offer to buy Great Western Financial Corp., whose stock surged 10-3/4 to 45.

"The Ahmanson premium represents three times book value so maybe we're at a new high in terms of what one is willing to pay for these thrifts," said Richard Cripps, chief market strategist at Legg Mason Wood Walker.
"But these deals are very much stock driven, so yes we're in a high market but if your currency is stock, perhaps the price is not as much as it would appear," he said.
H.F. Ahmanson shares also jumped after news of the offer, closing at 44-7/8, up 4-3/8.

Other deals announced included Marriott International Inc.'s agreement to acquire Renaissance Hotel Group NV for $1.0 billion in cash, or $30 per share. The agreement nullified an $890 million deal Renaissance had previously reached with Doubletree Corp.
Marriott gained one to 56-1/4 and Renaissance rose 4-5/8 to 29-3/4, while Doubletree's stock added 2-1/2 to 43-1/8.
Horizon/CMS Healthcare Corp. rose 2-1/4 to 16-1/2 after agreeing to a stock swap acquisition by HealthSouth Corp., whose stock fell 2-1/8 to 41.

Evergreen Media Corp. lost 1-1/4 to 31-1/2 after the company announced it would acquire Chancellor Broadcasting Co. in an all-stock deal. The companies also said they plan to acquire 10 radio properties from Viacom Inc. for $1.075 billion after completing their merger.
Chancellor rose 1/16 to 28 and Viacom shares gained 1-5/8 to 35.
The Nasdaq Composite index fell 1.40 points to 1,365.79.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 7.81 to 816.29, a new high. The American Stock Exchange index rose 3.94 to 598.09.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 3.59 to 427.07, a new high. The average share was up 37 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was at a new high of 7,792.574, up 54.716, or 0.71 percent.
